name: What is the best bathroom remodel order of operations?

mainEntity.name: What sequence should a bathroom remodel follow from demolition to final inspection?
mainEntity.text: What sequence should a bathroom remodel follow from demolition to final inspection?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bathroom remodel works best when the sequence is controlled and logical. Planning and material selection should happen first, followed by demolition and any structural repairs. After that come rough plumbing and electrical, then inspections if required, then waterproofing, tile, paint, and the final installation of vanity, toilet, shower trim, mirrors, and glass. The sequence matters because many trades depend on the previous one being complete and approved. Homeowners often run into trouble when they try to install finishes before the wet work and inspections are done. A good contractor should be able to explain the project in phases and tell you where waiting is necessary so quality is not sacrificed for speed.
acceptedAnswer.description: The usual order is planning, demolition, rough plumbing and electrical, framing repairs, waterproofing, tile, paint, fixture installation, glass, and final punch list. Skipping steps or rushing waterproofing and inspection stages can create costly rework later.
